capabilities: Speak exactly one word per keypress, with repeat, previous and spell controls
Highlight the current word and scroll to keep it in view
Read rendered text while skipping Markdown syntax, frontmatter, links and embeds
Jump to any word by clicking it, or resume saved positions per note
Support foot pedals, clickers and touchscreens via remappable keys and a control bar
extras: Mobile support is flagged as not yet tested on real devices; beta versions install via BRAT. Works offline with no accounts, API keys or network requests. Includes a maintainer checklist for community directory submission.
motivation: The author built it for copying journal entries from Obsidian into a paper notebook, where looking up at the screen is slow and loses your place.
problem: Copying text from screen to paper means repeatedly looking away and losing your place; Obsidian has no word-by-word spoken reader for this.
summary: Key-advance text-to-speech reader that speaks a note one word at a time so you can copy it out by hand.
